newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up despite agreement in B.C. talks.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up despite agreement in B.C. talks.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher on light pre-weekend short covering despite word an agreement was reached between British Columbia forest companies and lumber workers, traders said.
Lumber futures closed $3.20 per tbf higher to $1.00 lower with Septembert up most at $346.90 and November up $1.30 at $342.00 per tbf.

Reports of a little better activity in the cash market after Slocan Forest Products Ltd announced they would be taking mills down for one week appeared to have more influence on futures than the B.C. agreement, they said.
"There may be a delayed effect from the labor news after the weekend," one trader said.
Early resistance was attributed to the continued weak undertone to cash. Production is still running above demand despite the Slocan cutback, they added.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $340 per tbf, off $2 from midweek and $6 under last Friday's level.
